name: Properties for PROV was generated by
abstract: Schema defining properties for documenting hardware or software used in the creation of a dataset. Defines properties: @type, prov:used.

sources.title: See Provenance for discovery in Implementation of metadata content items

description:
## PROV generated by properties

Defines a set of properties for specifying instruments or software used in the generation of  a described resource.  Uses terms from the base prov vocabulary. For the schema.org implementation of the [Cross Domain Interoperability Framework](https://cross-domain-interoperability-framework.github.io/cdifbook/metadata/schemaorgimplementation.html#implementation-of-metadata-content-items) (CDIF) discovery profile.

examples.title: Example PROV was generated by.
examples.content: very simple implementation for discovery-level representation of instruments or software used to generate a resource.

annotatedSchema:
$schema: https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema
title: very simple links or names of software or instruments used to generate a resource.
type: object
required:
- '@type'
properties:
  '@type':
    type: array
    items:
      type: string
    minItems: 1
    contains:
      const: prov:Activity
  prov:used:
    type: array
    description: Entities the activity used. Per PROV-O each value denotes a prov:Entity.
      An item may be (1) a string URI or free-text reference, (2) an {@id} reference,
      (3) an inline entity object carrying an @type that includes prov:Entity plus
      a schema.org type for the kind of thing used, e.g. ["prov:Entity","schema:Thing"]
      (instrument), ["prov:Entity","schema:CreativeWork"] (method/protocol), or ["prov:Entity","schema:SoftwareApplication"]
      (software), or (4) a role-keyed wrapper naming what was used through one of
      the recognized "used" relations (schema:instrument, bios:computationalTool,
      bios:reagent), or (5) a role-keyed wrapper under a role a consuming profile
      defines for itself, admitted by shape rather than by name. Base leaves the wrapped
      value loose; profiles/extensions (e.g. cdifProvActivity, adaProduct) pin its
      shape (Instrument, ComputationalTool, Reagent, ...) and close the set of role
      names they accept.
    items:
      anyOf:
      - type: string
      - description: a resolvable reference to a representation of the software or
          instrument used
        $ref: https://cross-domain-interoperability-framework.github.io/metadataBuildingBlocks/build/annotated/bbr/metadata/cdifDataType/objectReference/schema.yaml
      - type: object
        description: an inline prov:Entity used by the activity (see prov:used description)
        properties:
          '@type':
            type: array
            items:
              type: string
            minItems: 1
            contains:
              const: prov:Entity
        required:
        - '@type'
      - type: object
        description: a role-keyed wrapper naming an instrument used by the activity;
          the extension layer pins the value to an Instrument description.
        required:
        - schema:instrument
      - type: object
        description: a role-keyed wrapper naming a computational tool (software) used;
          the extension layer pins the value to a ComputationalTool description.
        required:
        - bios:computationalTool
      - type: object
        description: a role-keyed wrapper naming a reagent / material used; the extension
          layer pins the value to a Reagent description.
        required:
        - bios:reagent
      - type: object
        description: 'a role-keyed wrapper under a role name this layer does not recognize:
          an object carrying at least one prefixed-name (CURIE) property other than
          @id / @type, whose value is an {@id} reference, an inline description, or
          an array of either. CDIF deliberately does NOT enumerate profile-defined
          roles here: the three named above (schema:instrument, bios:computationalTool,
          bios:reagent) are in CDIF/bioschemas scope and stay explicit, while a domain
          profile is free to relate an activity to what it used through a role of
          its own without CDIF having to know the term. A consuming profile is expected
          to CLOSE the set to the roles it defines, so this branch is permissive BY
          DESIGN at the base layer and the restriction returns at the profile layer.
          allOf composes correctly in that direction -- base permissive, profile restrictive
          -- because an allOf intersection can only narrow: a role this layer admits
          by shape is still rejected by any profile that does not name it.'
        minProperties: 1
        propertyNames:
          pattern: ^(@id|@type|[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*:[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*)$
        not:
          description: '@id / @type alone is the plain {@id} reference branch, not
            a wrapper; at least one property here must be a role.'
          propertyNames:
            enum:
            - '@id'
            - '@type'
        patternProperties:
          ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*:[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$:
            anyOf:
            - type: object
              description: an {@id} reference to, or an inline description of, the
                entity used in this role
            - type: array
              minItems: 1
              items:
                type: object
    x-jsonld-id: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov#used
x-jsonld-prefixes:
  schema: http://schema.org/
  prov: http://www.w3.org/ns/prov#
x-bblocks-metadata:
  itemIdentifier: cdif.bbr.metadata.provProperties.generatedBy
  register: https://cross-domain-interoperability-framework.github.io/metadataBuildingBlocks/build/register.json
  version: '0.1'
  dateOfLastChange: '2026-10-28'
